text:
riley: Heads up — canary batch jobs in eu-west1 started showing elevated allreduce latency and intermittent hangs after NCCL 2.25.1 package landed on the canary nodes. Started ~06:10 UTC.

matt: Any failures in dmesg or nv_peer_memory? Did the install also touch the driver/kernel?

riley: Quick grab from the failing pod: 
```
[2026-03-17T06:12:45Z] nccl WARN Call to ncclAllReduce hung: op=allreduce, root=0, timeout=120s
[2026-03-17T06:12:46Z] cudaLaunchKernel failed: unknown error (code=46)
[2026-03-17T06:12:47Z] kworker/3:2: nv_peer_mem: peer write failed, rc=-22
```

jana: How many jobs affected? Is it only 4xA100 profiles or also 8x?

riley: So far primarily 4x A100 inference shards (seq len typical), 6 separate allocations timed out across 3 nodes. One 8x job showed a pause but recovered.

sam: What are the exact stack: CUDA / driver / kernel / rdma libs on canaries? We had a driver bump in the canary image last week.

riley: Canary node image diffs: NCCL 2.25.1, libnccl 2.25.1-1, CUDA runtime 11.8.0, NVIDIA driver 525.85.06, kernel 5.15.0-70-generic, rdma-core 35.0.

matt: Driver 525.85.06 + NCCL 2.25.1 is a combo we didn't validate at scale. Suspect a P2P/peer memory regression with our NVLINK topology.

infra-bot: Deploy note: canary rollout was 10% of eu-west1 pool at 05:50 UTC — automation rolled back to previous packages for non-canary nodes. :information_source:

jana: Do we have perf traces? can we get an allreduce trace + nccl debug logs (set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO/TRACE) for a reproducer?

riley: Grabbed nccl logs from one repro node (trimmed):
```
NCCL INFO: using comm 0x7f9b2c, ring 0 -> 1
NCCL WARN: allreduce timeout, retrying (retry_count=3)
NCCL ERROR: collAbort triggered, aborting stream
Traceback (most recent call last): ...
```

sam: If we can reproduce, we should test two mitigations quickly: 1) roll driver back to 525.60.x (known-good) with NCCL 2.25.1; 2) rollback NCCL to 2.23.4 on canaries. Which is less invasive?

matt: Rolling NCCL is cheaper and faster to revert in our package manager. Driver changes touch node-level and require reboots. Start with NCCL rollback for the canary subset.

riley: I patched one canary pool to nccl 2.23.4 and kicked a few jobs — initial signs look good: no hangs in last 45m, latency back to baseline.

jana: Good. What's the impact on capacity if we pause the full rollout? Any cost hit?

matt: If we hold the rollout, capacity unaffected but we can't take advantage of optimization kernels from the new NCCL. If we rollback fleet-wide we need a coordinated package push — short outage windows for node restarts if driver changes needed.

sam: Action plan:
- Expand rollback to remaining canaries for NCCL to 2.23.4 (riley)
- Run targeted repros with NCCL_DEBUG=TRACE on 4x and 8x A100 jobs (matt)
- Schedule a deeper root cause (rdma/peer-mem/udmabuf) with NVIDIA if repros persist (jana)
- Hold driver upgrades until we have a validated matrix (ops)

riley: Doing NCCL rollback now, will report back in 30m. tagging @oncall for awareness. :eyes:

infra-bot: Rolling back nccl -> 2.23.4 on canary nodes (eu-west1-canary-group). Jobs will reschedule automatically.

matt: Also FYI — if rollback doesn't clear the hangs we'll throttle canary traffic (scale to 0) to avoid tail lat explosion and cost burn.

jana: Thanks. Keep notes in the incident doc and we can convert to a postmortem if it affects prod.

riley: Update: 60m after rollback, no new hangs in canaries, allreduce p50/p95 latencies back to normal. Closing the canary ticket for now, leaving follow-up with NVIDIA for compatibility matrix.

sam: Nice work — we'll schedule qa validation for driver+nccl combos before next automated rollout.
